key_takeaways: Microsoft publicly adopts 'deterministic gates over markdown' harness-engineering framing (quoting Burke Holland) as official product positioning.
Aspire 13.2 ships TypeScript/C# AppHost as compiler-gated infrastructure definition — agents read source and verify via compilation, not YAML+docs.
`aspire start` + `--isolated` mode solves port conflicts for parallel agent workstreams — same problem our tmux+worktree setup addresses at a different layer.
CLI-exposed OpenTelemetry (traces, metrics, structured logs) becomes the agent feedback loop, replacing log-file copy-paste and human-in-the-loop validation.
`aspire init` bundles MCP server + agent skills by default — Big-Tech convergence on agent-native bootstrap ergonomics (parallel to `claude init`).

discoveries.name: .NET Aspire 13.2
discoveries.reason: First Big-Tech harness-engineering product launch; standalone tool entry justified. Covers AppHost as code-based infra, `aspire start`, `--isolated` mode, OTel CLI surface, MCP+skills in `aspire init`.

discoveries.name: microsoft/aspire (GitHub)
discoveries.reason: Source of truth for AppHost schema, MCP server implementation, OTel CLI plumbing. Needed to verify the post's claims and extract adoptable patterns.

discoveries.name: Burke Holland — 'Markdown is not the answer / deterministic gates' X post
discoveries.reason: The provenance quote Microsoft uses to frame the entire harness-engineering pitch. Belongs in our deterministic-gates / anti-Markdown stdlib references alongside Karpathy's LLM Wiki and 12 Factor Agents.

discoveries.name: Aspire — Getting Started / First App
discoveries.reason: Walkthrough of agent-native `aspire init` plus the bundled skills + MCP; confirms exact ergonomics pattern we could mirror in our orchestrator bootstrap.

patterns_to_adopt.target: Orchestrator tmux+worktree workers — currently we isolate filesystem via worktree but don't enforce unique ports for parallel E2E / dev server runs. Add a port-allocation primitive per worker window.

patterns_to_adopt.pattern: CLI-exposed OpenTelemetry as agent feedback surface
patterns_to_adopt.target: Expose a normalized `orchestrator telemetry` command (tail traces / last N metrics) so Claude Code workers can self-diagnose without reading raw log files. Could sit next to Chrome DevTools MCP as a second verification channel.

patterns_to_adopt.pattern: Bundle agent primitives (MCP + skills) in the init command
patterns_to_adopt.target: Our `./run-tmux.sh` bootstrap should optionally scaffold CLAUDE.md + .claude/skills + MCP server registrations in target projects by default, matching the 'day-zero agent-ready' ergonomics.

notes: Strategic context: this is the first Big-Tech (Microsoft) product launch that opens with the harness-engineering thesis in our exact vocabulary. Useful citation for conservative German enterprise buyers ('Microsoft is shipping this now'). Contrasts with our language-agnostic Claude Code + tmux + worktree approach — Aspire is deeply .NET/C#/TypeScript opinionated. Convergence with Lopopolo's AIE Europe keynote and Anthropic's long-running harness post confirms industry-wide shift from 'better models' to 'better harnesses'.
